summary: :has() selects an element based on what it contains. li:has(input:checked) means "a list item that has a checked input inside it", which lets you style a parent based on its children.
notes: The first two checklist rows are crossed out because their checkboxes are checked. Click a row in the preview to toggle it.
.card:has(.badge) gives only the Web track card an orange border, because only it contains a badge.
:has() takes any selector inside the parentheses, including states like :checked, :focus, and :invalid.
pitfall: Writing li input:checked when you mean the li. That selects the checkbox, not the row, so the row style never changes.
